summaries.text:
1. Conversation Overview:
- Primary Objectives:
  - User: “looking at plan.md, I need to build a node.js application to be able to download all of the lidar data locally to a storage location I specify, and also provide a usable endpoint/server that can provide access to that data over an api.”
  - Allow selection among every source in the document, geographically scoped acquisition and whole-source acquisition, destination selection, local storage, source discovery, boundary-based terrain queries.
  - “allow downloading data at the best/most precise resolutions available … but allow all resolutions and options for each source, and also make those options/resolutions available through our api.”
  - Inspect the consumer at `C:\Repos\gcsdev\GCS-Dev\Scorecarder` and provide a compatible interface.
  - “You are on autopilot... build and run the application, testing as you go, until you've got something ready for me to try.”
  - Required port: **3123**. Node.js hosting. Configuration in **.env**.
- Workspace: `C:\Repos\lidarserver`; initially contained only `plan.md`. Windows. Date supplied by user: 2026-10-31.
- No changes were made to Scorecarder. Its source and bundled executables were only inspected/reused.
- No application server has been started yet.
- No frontend control screen has been created yet; only API documentation HTML/JS now exists under public/.
- No subagents have been used.
- Latest user message requests this handoff summary only; after compaction, resume the original implementation rather than treating it as complete.

Applicable Working Instructions:
- Start with concise commentary; provide progress frequently (roughly every 30 seconds / 3–5 tools).
- Preface every tool batch with a one-sentence purpose/outcome update.
- Use `functions.apply_patch` for manual file edits. No shell-write tricks or Python file manipulation.
- After a substantive edit, the next action must be focused executable validation when available. Do not read broadly or continue editing before validation.
- After the latest API patch, dependencies were installed; **npm test must run next**.
- Use full current tests for validation, honoring persistent user preference for fresh/full builds, not partial rebuilds. Final verification should include `npm ci`, full tests, and syntax checks from source.
- Do not revert changes not authored here. No commits or branches requested.
- Do not spawn subagents unless explicitly authorized by user/instructions/applicable skills; execution-subagent preference is superseded by that restriction.
- Deferred browser/Playwright tools must be loaded with `tool_search` before use; do not search again for tools already loaded. None have been loaded yet.
- Must verify browser UI desktop/mobile when built. Start server on 3123 as requested; if occupied, do not silently ignore explicit port constraint.
- Must provide concise final self-contained outcome with URL, useful integration instructions/caveats, then `task_complete` after a brief summary. Do not call it while work/errors remain.
- File references in user-facing messages should use workspace-relative Markdown links.
- Memory inspected: `/memories/` contains `build-preferences.md`, `debugging.md`, empty session/repo directories. No new memory written.
- Skills read: `project-setup-info-local/SKILL.md`. No framework-specific scaffolding needed for this ESM Node application.
- `rg` executable is unavailable. Workspace file tools work; external source search used a PowerShell directory traversal excluding dependencies/builds.
- Terminal is PowerShell; use `@' ... '@ | node --input-type=module` for inline ESM checks, not Unix heredocs. Use sync for one-shot commands, async only for persistent server.

2. Technical Foundation:
- Runtime:
  - `node --version`: **v24.14.1**.
  - ESM JavaScript (`"type": "module"`), Node >=24.
  - Built-in `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync`; emits experimental warning but works.
  - Express 5. No transpilation/build artifacts needed.
- Architecture:
  - Government services are contacted only by acquisition/discovery/catalog-refresh/update jobs.
  - Terrain/asset/compatibility serving is local-only; missing files return explicit errors, never public-service fallback.
  - Raw files immutable and versioned by source/URL/revision hash.
  - Stream large files, do not load TB datasets into memory.
  - SQLite RTree spatial index, course associations, persisted acquisition plans, jobs/events, source metadata, storage roots/locations.
  - One durable top-level job runs at a time; download workers use configured concurrency (default 2).
  - Running jobs reset to queued at startup; partial downloads resumed with validators.
  - Processing outputs in separate course-scoped/versioned directories.
  - Native survey/raster precision separated from requested/resampled output cells. Unknown point-cloud spacing stays unknown.
  - “Best” retains coarser coverage needed to fill fine-resolution gaps.
- Dependencies currently in package.json:
  - `@fontsource/ibm-plex-sans ^5.2.0`
  - `@terraformer/arcgis ^2.2.0`
  - `@turf/turf ^7.2.0`
  - `cheerio ^1.1.0`
  - `cors ^2.8.5`
  - `dotenv ^17.2.0`
  - `express ^5.1.0`
  - `geotiff ^2.1.3`
  - `helmet ^8.1.0`
  - `ipaddr.js ^2.2.0`
  - `leaflet ^1.9.4`
  - `leaflet-draw ^1.0.4` (latest patch)
  - `lucide ^0.468.0`
  - `proj4 ^2.19.0`
  - `shpjs ^6.1.0`
  - `sharp ^0.34.5` (latest patch)
  - `swagger-ui-dist ^5.27.0`
  - `undici ^7.13.0`
  - `unzipper ^0.12.0`
  - `zod ^4.0.0`
  - `topojson-client ^3.1.0` (latest patch)
  - `world-atlas ^2.0.2` (latest patch)
  - Dev: `playwright ^1.56.0`, `supertest ^7.1.0`.
- Scripts:
  - `start`: `node src/server.js`
  - `dev`: `node --watch src/server.js`
  - `test`: `node --test --test-concurrency=1 tests/*.test.js`
  - `check`: `node scripts/check.js`
- GIS tools:
  - Not on PATH initially.
  - Found existing complete Scorecarder environment:
    `C:/Repos/gcsdev/GCS-Dev/Scorecarder/setups/green-tools-env`
  - Executables in `Library/bin`.
  - Verified actual versions:
    - GDAL **3.13.2 "Iowa City", released 2026/07/20**
    - PDAL **2.10.2**
  - Environment needed:
    - PATH prepends `Library/bin`, `bin`, env root
    - `GDAL_DATA=<root>/Library/share/gdal`
    - `PROJ_DATA` / `PROJ_LIB=<root>/Library/share/proj`
    - `PROJ_NETWORK=OFF`
    - `GDAL_NUM_THREADS=2`, `GDAL_CACHEMAX=256`.
  - `gdaldem --version` prints valid GDAL version to stdout but exits 1 with usage on stderr. Detector now recognizes valid version output despite that exit. Processing commands still reject nonzero exits.
  - No external tool installation or modification to Scorecarder was needed.
- Current .env:
  ```
  HOST=127.0.0.1
  PORT=3123
  STORAGE_ROOT=C:/Repos/lidarserver/terrain-data
  CATALOG_PATH=C:/Repos/lidarserver/data/catalog.sqlite
  DOWNLOAD_CONCURRENCY=2
  DOWNLOAD_RETRIES=3
  REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS=60000
  DOWNLOAD_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS=120000
  MAX_DISCOVERY_ASSETS=100000
  MIN_FREE_DISK_GB=1
  DEFAULT_BUFFER_METERS=500
  MAX_EXPORT_PIXELS=4096
  MAX_PROCESSING_PIXELS=100000000
  MAX_ARCHIVE_UNCOMPRESSED_GB=1024
  UPDATE_CHECK_DAYS=30
  API_KEY=
  CORS_ORIGINS=http://localhost:3123,http://127.0.0.1:3123
  ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS=false
  DOWNLOAD_ALLOWED_HOSTS=
  PDAL_BIN=<Scorecarder env>/Library/bin/pdal.exe
  GDALINFO_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdalinfo.exe
  GDALWARP_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdalwarp.exe
  GDAL_TRANSLATE_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdal_translate.exe
  GDAL_CONTOUR_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdal_contour.exe
  GDALDEM_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdaldem.exe
  OGR2OGR_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/ogr2ogr.exe
  GDALSRSINFO_BIN=<env>/Library/bin/gdalsrsinfo.exe
  GIS_ENV_ROOT=<env>
  ```
  All `<env>` above are fully expanded paths in actual file.
- Security:
  - Loopback default. Non-loopback HOST requires API_KEY at startup.
  - Bearer authentication when configured; health public.
  - CORS origin allowlist; untrusted origins rejected before writes.
  - Loopback Host-header validation guards DNS rebinding.
  - Network host allowlist includes government domains and public AWS/ArcGIS infrastructure.
  - Private/reserved addresses rejected, including IPv4-mapped IPv6. Undici custom DNS lookup pins connections to verified public addresses.
  - Every redirect revalidated, max five.
  - Nonstandard ports and embedded credentials blocked by default.
  - File serving checks real paths against registered roots; destination symlink escape checked.
  - Download tickets for authenticated UI file links (10 minutes, opaque 48-hex token); not yet browser-tested.

Plan Requirements Read In Full:
- Government sources: USGS 3DEP; Ontario GeoHub; NRCan HRDEM/CDEM; PEI; Alberta; BC; Nova Scotia; Quebec; Saskatchewan.
- Raw LAZ preferred, but DEM/DSM and other published products supported.
- Course metadata/boundary; suggested 500–1000m buffer.
- Canada/USA, province/state, course directories.
- Never overwrite raw files.
- DTM/DSM; 0.5/1/2m contour intervals; hillshade; slope.
- SQLite catalog, background jobs, Swagger.
- Offline repository and serving, 20TB+ scale.
- Monthly provider updates.
- Course endpoints `/api/course/{id}`, `/terrain`, assets, search.
- AI/hole terrain package exports; future imagery/centerline/hazard references.
- Separate generated artifacts.
- Frontend recommendation React/Leaflet/MapLibre; agent chose lightweight plain JS Leaflet frontend, not yet implemented.

Scorecarder Compatibility Evidence:
- Consumer module:
  `C:\Repos\gcsdev\GCS-Dev\Scorecarder\src\scorecards\lib\green-map-worker.js`
- Other inspected:
  - `src/scorecards/lib/green-map-toolchain.js`
  - `lidarsources.md`
  - `package.json`
- `normalizeAsset` accepts:
  - URL fields `url`, `href`, `downloadUrl`, `download_url`, `assetUrl`, `asset_url`
  - `source`, `title`, `bbox`/`bounds`, `extension`, `mediaType`, `cellSizeMeters`.
- Scorecarder bbox object:
  `{minLng, minLat, maxLng, maxLat}`.
- Processable URL must end in `.tif/.tiff/.las/.laz/.zlas` or extension supplied.
- Direct URL/manifests:
  - `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_TILE_URLS`
  - `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_MANIFEST_JSON`
  - `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_MANIFEST_FILE`
- ArcGIS catalog hook:
  `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ARCGIS_QUERY_URLS`
- STAC hooks:
  - `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_STAC_ENDPOINTS`
  - `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_STAC_COLLECTIONS`
- Ontario-specific ImageServer export existing; do not redirect it to an unimplemented local ImageServer proxy.
- Worker source selector `auto`, `ontario`, `nrcan-pei`, `quebec`, `manual`.
- Recommended compatible integration planned: `lidarSource: manual`, disable Ontario direct fallback, configure local ArcGIS query or local STAC/manifest.
- Worker ArcGIS query adds `/query`, WGS84 envelope geometry, outFields etc.; extracts URL attributes.
- Worker STAC search POSTs `{bbox, limit, collections}` and extracts item assets.
- Green very fine requested cells (0.025/0.05/0.1m) are not necessarily native precision; API explicitly separates these.
- Do not change Scorecarder without user authorization.

3. Codebase Status:
- `plan.md`:
  - Original user plan, unchanged.
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json`:
  - Full ESM app setup and dependencies.
  - Lock generated/updated by npm installs.
  - Latest install succeeded.
- `.gitignore`:
  ```
  node_modules/
  .env
  terrain-data/
  data/
  logs/
  test-results/
  *.log
  *.sqlite*
  *.part
  ```
- `.env`:
  - Actual local config described above.
  - `.env.example` not yet created.
- `src/spatial.js`:
  - Exports `HttpError`, `parseBbox`, `normalizeBoundary`, `intersectsBoundary`, `selectAssets`, `metricCrs`, `assetsGeojson`.
  - `parseBbox`: comma string, array, Scorecarder fields, west/south/east/north, or USGS minX/minY/maxX/maxY.
  - Rejects invalid extents and antimeridian crossing; asks to split request.
  - GeoJSON Polygon/MultiPolygon/Feature validation: closed rings, numeric WGS84, max100k coordinates.
  - Turf meter buffer, max10km.
  - Exact polygon intersection including holes.
  - Best mode groups source/product; ranks known meters or approximate arc-second spacing; retains unknown resolution; discards coarse tiles only when finer polygons completely cover the queried portion using Turf intersect/difference.
  - `all`/`native` keep all; numeric matches native/requested meters.
  - Metric CRS local UTM, polar fallback.
- `src/config.js`:
  - `projectRoot`, `loadConfig`, `persistStorageRoot`, `safeSegment`, `courseDirectory`, `isContained`.
  - Reads .env with dotenv. Numeric validation.
  - `.env` storage persistence uses dotenv parser, rewrites key/value JSON-quoted values atomically; retains unrelated settings, though comments/formatting aren’t preserved.
  - Writability probe, absolute paths required.
  - Folder pattern `<root>/canada|usa/<province or national>/<course id>`.
  - Latest additions: archive GB limit, gdalsrsinfo path.
- `src/catalog.js`:
  - `assetId(sourceId,url,revision)` SHA256 first32 hex.
  - `Catalog` SQLite:
    - sources/settings/storage_roots/courses/assets
    - RTree asset_bounds
    - course_assets
    - jobs/job_events
    - discovery_plans/packages
    - latest `asset_locations` table for preserving multiple destinations.
  - WAL/foreign keys/busy timeout.
  - Asset upsert preserves existing ready path/status when rediscovered remotely; revision changes produce distinct ID.
  - `markDownloaded` stores etag/lastModified in metadata and location row.
  - `queryAssets` uses RTree for boundary prefilter then Turf selection.
  - Default local-only; `localOnly:false` exposes remote catalog entries internally.
  - `saveCourse`, `course`, `courses`, `linkAsset`.
  - `savePlan`, `plan`.
  - `createJob`, `job`, `jobs`, `updateJob`, `event`, `events`.
  - `stats` converts SQL byte counts to Number, tested at25TB.
  - Latest `locations`, `setting`, `setSetting`, `pendingJob`.
- `src/network.js`:
  - `publicAddress`, `fileHash`, `publishFile`, class `Network`.
  - Undici Agent DNS/address validation; trusted domains.
  - `validateUrl`, `response`, `json`, `text`, `download`, `downloadAttempt`, `close`.
  - Redirect handling, HTTP/provider JSON errors.
  - Stream to `.part`; `.part.json` validators.
  - Resume only if URL and ETag/Last-Modified match stored metadata; `Range` + `If-Range`, verify Content-Range.
  - If server returns200, restart rather than append. 416 restarts.
  - Idle timeout reset per chunk, retries exponential cancellable delays.
  - Incremental SHA256, expected byte count/provider checksum, TIFF/BigTIFF/LASF/ZIP signatures.
  - HTML/JSON masquerading as terrain rejected (GeoJSON intentionally allowed).
  - Periodic disk reserve checks every64MB.
  - `publishFile`: hardlink temporary to final, then unlink; fallback exclusive copy for unsupported filesystems. Never overwrites raw destination.
  - Existing completed destination reused and rehashed.
- `src/gis.js`:
  - Proj4 definitions UTM north/south, NAD83 UTM1–23, EPSG3979 Canada Lambert, EPSG3413/3031 polar.
  - `projectExtent` densifies bbox perimeter to metric extent; `geographicExtent` transforms corners back.
  - `Gis.environment`, `run`, `check`.
  - Direct spawn `shell:false`; cancellation; timeouts; output cap64MB; error details stdout/stderr/code.
  - Valid gdaldem version recognized even nonzero version-command exit.
  - Actual processing failures remain fatal.
- `src/indexes.js`:
  - `attributeLinks`: structured HTML extraction with Cheerio or direct HTTP(S) values.
  - `extensionFor`, `attributeResolution`.
  - `canonicalDownloadUrl`: rewrites rejected `download-telecharger.services.geo.ca/pub/...` to `ftp.maps.canada.ca/pub/...`.
  - `geojsonFeatures`: Feature, FeatureCollection, Polygon/MultiPolygon support.
  - `extractArchive`: unzipper central directory, max entries/bytes, no traversal/absolute paths, exclusive extraction; existing size mismatch refuses overwrite.
  - `VectorIndexes.query`:
    - HEAD revision, hash versioned cache directory `.indexes/<source>/<hash>`.
    - network download index, extract if zip.
    - configured index filename or first vector file.
    - OGR spatial filter (`-spat_srs EPSG:4326 -spat ... -t_srs EPSG:4326`) to GeoJSON stdout.
    - GeoJSON direct parser.
    - SHP fallback with shpjs only if GIS missing.
    - exact boundary filtering; `fullGeometry` option for full federal footprint.
  - Potential future risk: extraction currently writes directly to member path; interrupted member can be partial and later mismatch. Test/repair if encountered; raw archive preserved.
- `src/sources.js`:
  - `builtInSources` nine entries:
    `ontario`, `nrcan`, `pei`, `bc`, `quebec`, `alberta`, `nova-scotia`, `saskatchewan`, `usgs-3dep`.
  - Each has homepage/license/coverage/collections/native options and honest notes.
  - Alberta/NS/SK automatic delivery via federal open CanElevation, not fictitious anonymously downloadable Altalis/provincial data. Custom adapters allow other verified government indexes.
  - `assetsFromFeatures`, `ontarioExports`, class `SourceRegistry`.
  - `SourceRegistry`: list/get aliases (`nrcan-pei→pei`, `usgs→usgs-3dep`), options, refresh, arcgisFeatures, stacAssets, usgsAssets, discover, register.
  - Constructor merges built-in updated definitions into existing cached sources while retaining refreshed provider metadata/new collections.
  - ArcGIS complete enumeration:
    - `returnIdsOnly=true`
    - chunks500 IDs
    - checks transfer truncation
    - ImageServer uses JSON (not GeoJSON); others GeoJSON
    - Terraformer handles ArcGIS geometry.
  - STAC pagination GET search, next GET/POST body, loop detection, only data-role supported files.
  - NRCan checks actual extent.geojson per project; handles single Feature; filters out neighboring project rectangle overlap.
  - Native resolution from GSD/collection/proj transform; provider metadata kept.
  - USGS all products pagination, boundingBox minX etc., size metadata.
  - Discover supports `scope:source` or bbox/polygon, products, formats, collections, delivery, best/all/native/numeric.
  - Default products DTM. Default Ontario export rather than massive packages; PEI DTM tiles and Quebec MNT index rather than whole-project mosaics.
  - Complete/partial plan warnings/errors persisted; no silent limit truncation.
  - Custom arcgis/stac/vector requires id/name/license/coverage/collections and trusted URLs.
- `src/processing.js`:
  - `pointCloudPipeline`, `rasterMetadata`, class `TerrainProcessor`.
  - PDAL per-source reader/reprojection tags, explicit merge, metric crop.
  - DTM ground Classification==2 (unless groundOnly false).
  - DSM rejects noise classifications7/18 and uses max.
  - Optional point-cloud zScale.
  - GDAL tiled/compressed BigTIFF outputs.
  - Archive expansion/indexing of rasters/point-cloud files.
  - `process` local inputs only, course/explicit boundary, max pixels explicit no silent coarsening.
  - Resolution preserves finest native raster, default0.5 for point-cloud unknown.
  - Cutline GeoJSON, local metric CRS.
  - Raster mosaic order coarse first/fine last, oldest first/newer last for equal cells.
  - Produces DTM/DEM base, optional DSM, contours0.5/1/2 with elevation attr and OGR WGS84, multidirectional/classic hillshade, slope degrees/percent.
  - Does not fabricate DSM from ground-only raster; warning explicit.
  - Source vertical datum retained, no automatic vertical harmonization.
  - Immutable generated outputs under `<course>/dem|contours|hillshade|slope/<job id>/`.
  - Working pipelines/cutline under `<course>/generated/jobs/<job id>/`.
  - Catalog entries/provenance, course associations and generated terrain manifest.
  - Progress total corrected for three contour variants.
  - Potential remaining issue: resumed processing job can encounter existing intermediate filenames; current real test validates fresh run, not restart mid-processing.
- `src/jobs.js`:
  - `JobManager extends EventEmitter`.
  - Types: discover/download/acquire/process/extract/refresh/updates.
  - Persistent queue; interrupted running→queued.
  - Emits change/settled/idle. `enqueue`, `wake`, `drain`, `cancel`, `stop`.
  - Download plan rejects incomplete discovery unless `allowPartial:true`.
  - Destination snapshot in payload; root registered; country/province/course raw paths.
  - Parallel workers, progress/transfers/logs, completed files kept when others fail.
  - Local copy to new root with SHA validation, retains old file; location table tracks both.
  - Download TIFF metadata then link to course.
  - `processAfterDownload` option.
  - Monthly/manual `checkUpdates`: refresh metadata, HEAD compare ETag/Last-Modified, new immutable revision entries; download changed only if requested.
  - Unknown validators reported unknown, not assumed current.
- **Latest, not yet validated** `src/terrain.js`:
  - `TerrainReader.pathFor` realpath against catalog roots and alternate locations; explicit missing/disconnected-volume error.
  - GeoTIFF local reading, proj4 CRS or offline gdalsrsinfo lookup.
  - `sample`, `elevations` up to1000 WGS84 points, fine-first/newer-first fallback when nodata.
  - `grid`: bounded max512×512, north-to-south WGS84 layout, projected source-window sampling, null nodata, min/max/provenance.
  - `preview`: locally generated PNG with Sharp raw RGBA; source colors/alpha handled explicitly.
- **Latest, not yet validated** `src/openapi.js`:
  - Generates OpenAPI3.1 document with main service/source/acquisition/jobs/course/terrain/assets/compatibility routes.
  - Bearer security scheme only required if configured.
  - Native precision/offline contract described.
- **Latest, not yet validated** `src/app.js`:
  - `createService(overrides)` builds config/catalog/network/GIS/registry/jobs/reader/Express; returns all with async close.
  - Zod request schema and helpers:
    - `list`, `base`, `urlFor`, `publicAsset`, `optionsFor`, `page`, `queue`, `courseFor`, `terrainFor`.
  - `publicAsset` hides filesystem path; local URLs end `/download.<ext>` for Scorecarder; bbox object and cellSizeMeters provided.
  - Routes:
    - `/api/health`
    - GET/PATCH `/api/settings`
    - GET `/api/storage/directories`
    - GET `/api/tools`
    - GET/POST `/api/sources`
    - GET `/api/sources/:id`, `/options`, `/assets`
    - POST `/api/sources/:id/discover`
    - POST `/api/discover`, GET `/api/discovery/:id`
    - POST `/api/downloads`, `/api/acquire`
    - GET `/api/jobs`, `/:id`, `/:id/events`
    - POST jobs `/refresh`, `/updates`, `/process`, `/extract`, `/:id/cancel`, `/:id/retry`
    - GET/POST `/api/courses`, GET `/api/search`
    - GET/PUT `/api/course/:id`, GET `/terrain`, `/manifest`
    - POST `/api/course/:id/package`, GET `/api/packages/:id`
    - GET/POST `/api/terrain/query`, GET `/footprints`
    - GET/POST `/api/terrain/elevation`, GET `/grid`
    - GET `/api/assets/:id`, `/download.:extension`, `/metadata`, `/preview.png`
    - POST `/api/assets/:id/ticket`, GET `/api/downloads/:token/:filename`
    - GET/POST `/api/scorecarder/manifest`
    - GET `/api/scorecarder/query` ArcGIS shape, no truncation
    - `/api/stac`, `/collections`, `/collections/:id/items`, `/items/:id`, GET/POST `/search`
    - `/api/openapi.json`
    - `/api/map/land`: local world-atlas countries converted via topojson-client
    - `/docs`, vendor assets, static public, favicon204.
  - File streaming via Express sendFile, Range/ETag/immutable caching.
  - Browser origin/Host/auth guards.
  - Local map/vendor URLs:
    - `/vendor/leaflet` → node_modules/leaflet/dist
    - `/vendor/draw` → leaflet-draw/dist
    - `/vendor/lucide` → lucide/dist/umd
    - `/vendor/fonts` → @fontsource/ibm-plex-sans
    - `/vendor/swagger` → swagger-ui-dist
  - CSP allows only self scripts/connect/fonts, self/data/blob images and OSM tiles, inline styles for Leaflet/Swagger.
  - Monthly timer checks once/hour, queues updates after configured days; no automatic bulk changed downloads.
  - Default storage PATCH blocked while active job, persists .env and keeps prior roots.
  - Potential risks to check via tests:
    - Express5 behavior/route patterns.
    - GeoTIFF writeArrayBuffer fixture decode.
    - grid and preview sampling.
    - gdalsrsinfo version detection after adding eighth tool.
    - STAC collections items handler mutates `request.query.collections` although Express5 query is a getter; extra explicit source filter means mutation unnecessary.
    - Source-scoped STAC collection coverage for `derived` not advertised.
    - source registration input validation is partly manual.
    - No server/UI first-screen route content yet.
- **Latest** `src/server.js`:

+# TerrainServer
+
+Node.js terrain acquisition and local-only serving for Canada and the United States. Select government providers, draw/import a WGS84 boundary or enumerate a whole source, review the acquisition plan, and store immutable files at your chosen destination. A local Leaflet control screen, REST API, STAC search, and Scorecarder-compatible catalog expose the downloaded data.
+
+## Run
+
+Requires Node.js **24+**. There is no transpilation step; the server runs directly from the JavaScript source.
+
+```powershell
+npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
+npm run check
+npm test
+npm start
+```
+
+The control screen is **http://127.0.0.1:3123/** and interactive API documentation is **http://127.0.0.1:3123/docs**.
+
+The current local [.env](.env) is configured for `C:/Repos/lidarserver/terrain-data` and the existing GDAL/PDAL installation under `C:/Repos/gcsdev/GCS-Dev/Scorecarder/setups/green-tools-env`. That installation is reused without modifying Scorecarder. For another machine, use [.env.example](.env.example) as the configuration reference and adjust the executable and storage paths.
+
+GDAL and PDAL are required for terrain generation and some vector indexes. The GUI's **Repository Settings** shows tool availability. Tools must include GeoTIFF, GeoPackage, Shapefile, LAS/LAZ, and projection support. `GIS_ENV_ROOT` supplies the library, GDAL data, and PROJ paths for a contained environment; projection-network access remains disabled.
+
+Windows browser tests use installed Microsoft Edge. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL` in `.env` for another installed browser channel. On other platforms, install the bundled test browser with `npx playwright install chromium`. Real GIS tests require the configured tools; unavailable toolchains are reported rather than mocked as successful processing.
+
+## First Trial
+
+The repository includes **Ontario Sample Area**, a small, explicitly labeled test area near Toronto, not a claimed golf-course boundary. A real native 0.5 m Ontario DTM was acquired through the GUI. DTM, contours at 0.5/1/2 m intervals, hillshade, and slope were generated locally.
+
+1. Open **Repository** to inspect or download the local files.
+2. Open **Courses**, then use the map icon beside Ontario Sample Area to select its boundary.
+3. In **Acquire**, choose sources, products, resolutions, delivery/collection options, and a destination. **Discover Files** creates a reviewable plan without downloading terrain files.
+4. Review sizes, native grids, coverage, and provider warnings, then download all or selected files. Job details show progress, logs, cancellation, and retry controls.
+5. Use the terrain-generation icon in **Courses** to create new, versioned outputs from complete local inputs.
+
+On an empty installation, select **Ontario sample area** from the area selector, then save it as a course. Its zero-meter buffer is intentional for a very small trial. Normal course buffers default to 500 m and can be configured up to 10,000 m.
+
+The map uses bundled country geometry by default. OpenStreetMap is an optional online basemap. Provider discovery/refresh requires Internet access, but existing terrain downloads, previews, elevation/grid queries, and catalogs never contact government services as a fallback.
+
+## Sources And Precision
+
+| Source | Automatic open-data delivery |
+| --- | --- |
+| Ontario GeoHub | Clipped native 0.5 m DTM exports, DTM/DSM packages, classified point-cloud tile links |
+| NRCan CanElevation | HRDEM project and national mosaics, Arctic DEM, CDEM, MRDEM, classified point clouds |
+| Prince Edward Island | 2020 native 1 m DTM tiles, federal DTM/DSM surveys, federal point clouds |
+| LidarBC | Provincial DEM/DSM and point-cloud indexes; actual per-tile spacing is retained |
+| Quebec | Provincial native MNT/DTM tile index plus federal DSM/point-cloud coverage |
+| Alberta | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Alberta |
+| Nova Scotia | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Nova Scotia |
+| Saskatchewan | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Saskatchewan |
+| USGS 3DEP | LPC, 1 m/seamless DEMs, published arc-second DEMs, Alaska products, contours |
+
+Alberta/NS/SK account-gated, paid, or unverified provincial delivery is **not** presented as anonymous open downloads. Some Ontario point-cloud tiles require ordering. Coverage is uneven; provider failures and missing anonymous links are recorded in the acquisition plan. Custom ArcGIS, STAC, and vector-index sources can be registered through the GUI or `POST /api/sources` using verified endpoints and attribution.
+
+`GET /api/sources/:id/options` exposes products, collections, formats, delivery modes, known native raster grids, and provider export options. Refreshing provider catalogs adds newly published collection metadata. Provincial choices distinguish native tile grids from dataset scale labels, such as BC's 1:2500 index.
+
+- `best`: prefer the finest known native grid per source/product, retaining coarser tiles needed to fill coverage gaps and point clouds with unknown spacing.
+- `all`: retain all published resolutions, deliveries, and survey variants matching the selected products and collections.
+- `native`: retain native grids without inventing finer survey precision. Default delivery preferences still apply unless you select collections/delivery explicitly.
+- A numeric `resolution`: select a matching native grid; Ontario clipped exports can also request a custom output cell. Finer output cells are explicitly marked **resampled**, not new survey precision.
+
+Raw point-cloud density is not a raster cell size. Unknown spacing/density remains unknown. Meter-grid and angular-resolution products are distinguished. Terrain processing can request arbitrary positive output cells within the configured pixel limit; finer cells interpolate existing observations. Elevation responses retain declared units and vertical-datum provenance. Unknown units are returned as `source units`; no vertical-datum harmonization or inferred unit conversion is performed. `zScale` can explicitly scale point-cloud heights.
+
+Whole-source Ontario acquisition defaults to native packages. Clipped ImageServer exports require an area boundary. Whole-source jobs can be extremely large; inspect known bytes and unknown-size counts before downloading. `MAX_DISCOVERY_ASSETS` and pixel limits fail explicitly instead of silently truncating enumeration or coarsening data. Raise these limits deliberately for larger acquisitions.
+
+## Storage And Jobs
+
+Change the default location through the folder shortcut or Repository Settings. It is persisted to `.env`; all prior roots remain registered and their files are preserved. Each job snapshots its destination. The acquisition form can override the destination for that job without changing the default. Use an absolute local, external-drive, or UNC path with write permission.
+
+```text
+terrain-data/
+  canada|usa/
+    province-or-state|national/
+      course-id|repository/
+        metadata.json
+        course_boundary.geojson
+        lidar/raw/<source>-<immutable-asset-id>.laz
+        dem/raw/<source>-<immutable-asset-id>.tif
+        dem/<processing-job-id>/dtm.tif
+        contours/<processing-job-id>/...
+        hillshade/<processing-job-id>/...
+        slope/<processing-job-id>/...
+        generated/jobs/<job-id>/...
+        ai/terrain-package-<id>.json
+  .indexes/<source>/<revision>/...
+```
+
+SQLite stores RTree footprints, metadata, course associations, source options, discovery plans, jobs, logs, and registered file locations. Keep the catalog on a reliable local disk; terrain files may reside on other registered volumes. Back up the catalog and `.env` with the raw data, using a SQLite-aware backup or stopping the server before copying the database and its journal files.
+
+Downloads stream to `.part` files, resume with ETag/Last-Modified and verified range responses, validate signatures/lengths and SHA-256, and publish without overwriting an existing raw path. Provider revisions receive distinct IDs. Copying a catalog asset to another destination retains its previous location. A disconnected volume produces an explicit local-file error; it does not trigger an online fallback.
+
+One durable top-level job runs at a time; downloads use the configured worker concurrency. Running jobs become queued after restart, completed raw files remain intact, and retries resume partial transfers. Cancellation preserves completed and partial files. Interrupted processing may leave working files for inspection; a retry creates a new versioned processing job. Archive extraction preserves the raw ZIP and enforces traversal and uncompressed-size limits. Proprietary ZLAS is downloadable but must be converted externally before processing.
+
+Monthly checks refresh provider metadata and compare validators on acquired assets. They **do not automatically download changed terrain**. `POST /api/jobs/updates` with `downloadChanged: true` explicitly queues changed files. Missing validators are reported as unknown freshness.
+
+Large raw files are streamed; previews use internal overviews or bounded local GDAL windows. Course processing is spatially/pixel bounded, not a whole-country processing batch. This implementation is designed for large repositories, but a 20 TB acquisition/storage stress test has not been performed. Monitor disk space, native-tool memory, and provider limits during large deployments. Catalog byte totals count each current asset once; replicas, index caches, and intermediate working files are additional disk usage.
+
+## REST Examples
+
+Swagger contains request schemas and the full endpoint list. Core routes include:
+
+| Route | Purpose |
+| --- | --- |
+| `GET /api/sources` and `/:id/options` | Cached source metadata and native options |
+| `POST /api/discover` | Queue discovery; inspect job result `planId` |
+| `GET /api/discovery/:id` | Paginated plan, warnings, native metadata, and all asset IDs |
+| `POST /api/downloads` | Download a plan or selected asset IDs |
+| `POST /api/acquire` | Explicit discovery and download in one durable job |
+| `GET /api/jobs/:id` and `/events` | Status, progress, result, and cursor-based logs |
+| `GET/POST /api/courses` | Search/register WGS84 course boundaries |
+| `GET /api/course/:id/terrain` | Local DEM/DTM/DSM, contours, hillshade, and slope URLs |
+| `GET/POST /api/terrain/query` | Local assets filtered by boundary, source, product, grid, or course |
+| `GET /api/assets/:id/download.tif` | Local byte-range/ETag streaming; use the actual extension |
+| `POST /api/terrain/elevation` | Up to 1,000 WGS84 `[longitude, latitude]` points |
+| `GET /api/terrain/grid?assetId=...` | Up to 512x512 cells, north-to-south, WGS84 cell centers |
+| `POST /api/jobs/process` | Generate local course/area terrain products |
+| `POST /api/course/:id/package` | Export a persisted AI/hole package with local asset URLs |
+
+PowerShell discovery example:
+
+```powershell
+$body = @{
+  sourceIds = @('ontario')
+  products = @('dtm')
+  bbox = @(-79.52, 43.64, -79.519, 43.641)
+  bufferMeters = 0
+  resolution = 'best'
+  delivery = 'export'
+  courseId = 'ontario-sample-area'
+} | ConvertTo-Json
+$job = Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/discover -Method Post -ContentType application/json -Body $body
+Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/jobs/$($job.id)"
+```
+
+Once that job is completed, use its `progress.result.planId` in:
+
+```json
+{
+  "planId": "<completed-plan-id>",
+  "storageRoot": "D:/TerrainData",
+  "courseId": "ontario-sample-area",
+  "processAfterDownload": true,
+  "processing": {
+    "products": ["dtm", "contours", "hillshade", "slope"],
+    "contourIntervals": [0.5, 1, 2]
+  }
+}
+```
+
+Send that body to `POST /api/downloads`. Incomplete plans are refused unless you explicitly set `allowPartial: true`. Asset query/plan pages use `offset` and `limit` (maximum 1,000); responses include `total` and `nextOffset`. Bboxes accept arrays, comma-separated strings, or Scorecarder's `{minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat}` shape. Polygon/MultiPolygon holes are respected. Antimeridian-crossing requests must be split.
+
+Packages can optionally reference a **previously local** satellite asset and include hole, hazards, centerline, or green geometry. There is no satellite acquisition or golf-feature AI inference engine. Packages expose the available terrain and supplied references, not invented geometry.
+
+## Scorecarder Integration
+
+Scorecarder's existing `green-map-worker.js` consumes compatible asset fields and URL extensions. No Scorecarder files were changed. Use its existing configuration hooks:
+
+```dotenv
+SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_SOURCE=manual
+SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ONTARIO_DTM_ENABLED=false
+SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ONTARIO_DTM_PER_GREEN_ENABLED=false
+SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ARCGIS_QUERY_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/scorecarder/query
+```
+
+Remove other remote ArcGIS/STAC hooks, tile URLs, and old remote manifests when you require the consumer to remain local-only. `manual` avoids its built-in government source discovery; disabling both Ontario flags avoids direct ImageServer exports. The local ArcGIS hook accepts the worker's WGS84 envelope and returns `downloadUrl`, `source`, `title`, `bbox`, `extension`, and `cellSizeMeters`, without a transfer-limit truncation.
+
+Alternative hooks:
+
+- Local STAC: `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_STAC_ENDPOINTS=http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/stac` with optional source collections such as `ontario,nrcan,pei,bc,quebec,usgs-3dep,derived`.
+- Manifest: obtain `GET /api/scorecarder/manifest?bbox=...` or `GET /api/course/:id/manifest`, follow pagination when applicable, and pass the JSON to its existing `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_MANIFEST_JSON` or manifest-file hook. The hook expects JSON/file contents, not a remote manifest URL.
+
+Acquire the requested course/green area first. The consumer receives only complete local processable TIFF/LAS/LAZ assets; ZIP/ZLAS/IMG can remain raw and need extraction/conversion as appropriate. Finer Scorecarder output cells do not imply finer source surveys.
+
+The existing consumer hooks do not add TerrainServer Bearer headers automatically. The default loopback/no-key configuration works directly. When enabling `API_KEY`, add authenticated requests in the consumer or use a trusted authenticated integration layer; do not put an API key into a catalog URL. Direct browser clients also need their actual origin added to `CORS_ORIGINS`. Server-to-server requests are not subject to browser CORS.
+
+## Security And Operations
+
+Loopback binding is the default. A non-loopback `HOST` requires `API_KEY`, and authenticated callers can browse storage paths and queue downloads, so treat that key as administrative access. Bind behind TLS and firewall restrictions for remote use. The GUI keeps the key only in page memory; downloaded-file tickets expire after ten minutes. API definition/health and static frontend assets are public, but repository data/settings require Bearer authentication when enabled.
+
+Download destinations are checked against registered roots and real paths. Public-source network requests reject private/reserved IPs, unexpected hosts/ports, embedded credentials, and unsafe redirects, with validated DNS connection addresses. `DOWNLOAD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` extends the government/public-infrastructure allowlist. `ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS` is an explicit development/trusted-internal exception; do not enable it for untrusted callers. Native tools are spawned directly without a shell. Provider content is data, not executable instructions.
+
+Keep provider attribution with reused raw and derived data. `.env`, the terrain/index files, catalogs, dependencies, and logs are ignored by Git. Do not delete registered raw files to free space without accounting for dependent course/derived manifests. Shut down with Ctrl+C so the current job is persisted for restart.
*** End Patch","explanation":"Document setup, all source/resolution options, full-source safety, immutable storage and jobs, API usage, offline behavior, exact Scorecarder hooks, authentication, and portable .env configuration."}

- Map Source includes a `Whole-Hole 3D Terrain` section after Hole Display Boundaries and before Green Detail Editor.
- Each hole uses its saved display boundary when present, with the mapped tee-to-green route plus padding as a fallback.
- The section duplicates the applicable LiDAR source, ground filtering, point-cloud interpolation, detail, contour, and shading controls with whole-hole defaults.

- Whole-hole defaults are a 1 m requested DEM cell, 1 m minor contours, 5 m major contours, and a 192 x 192 maximum browser mesh. Large extents automatically use a coarser effective cell size to stay under that cap.
- Three.js renders the terrain interactively with satellite imagery, optional contour overlays, optional terrain shading, and adjustable vertical exaggeration.

- Whole-hole 3D views rotate each route so the green is at the top and tees are at the bottom. The default view uses 3.5x vertical exaggeration, a detailed 256-side mesh cap, 30% contour brightness, and hole isolation that darkens imagery outside the selected tee-to-green corridor.

- Whole-hole isolation assigns mapped fairways, tees, greens, bunkers, rough, and water features to their nearest numbered hole route, sizes route-fallback terrain around that owned feature union, and preserves a 32 m rough/tree context around the connected playing corridor. Adjacent-hole features are excluded by nearest-route ownership.

- Generated files are stored under the existing course-scoped green-map work root in `hole-terrain/`, then packaged as `hole-terrain-plan.json`, `hole-terrain-products.json`, and `hole-terrain/hole-XX/*` in legacy and basemap packages.

- Green and bunker detail behavior is intentionally unchanged. Green generation continues to default to a 0.05 m DEM cell with 0.1 m minor and 0.5 m major contours; whole-hole options never flow into the green-map plan or products.

- Green Detail can render the generated green DEM as a satellite-textured 3D mesh with green-up orientation, 3.5x default height, and adjustable low-brightness contours. Its browser grid is downsampled to at most 256 samples per side without changing source DEM or contour resolution.

- Green shading generation/export supports `classic` color relief or `new` multidirectional natural hill shading. Offline Map Pack exposes the choice and regenerates the selected style before packaging; both styles retain the same contour intervals, and green terrain grids are included in legacy and split green-data archives.

Scorecarder needs selectable elevation/LiDAR sources so Green Detail generation can work outside Ontario. Ontario remains as-is: the existing `ontario-dtm-lidar-derived-imageserver` integration is still the preferred Ontario default. The rest of Canada should be added through source connectors that can discover a course bounding box, return downloadable DEM/DTM rasters or point-cloud tiles, and feed the existing GDAL/PDAL worker.
The current worker already has useful generic hooks:
That means the implementation should not rewrite contour generation. It adds a source selector and source-specific discovery adapters that produce the same asset list the worker already understands.
Add a Green Detail control named `Elevation source` with these initial choices:
- Try Ontario DTM when the course bbox intersects Ontario.
- Try federal HRDEM/CanElevation 1 m DTM for all Canadian bboxes.
- Fall back to manual manifest/direct URL selection.
- Current behavior; leave as-is and keep Ontario-only bbox gating.
- Other provinces as they become reliable.
- For municipalities, private captures, or one-off provincial downloads.

The selected source is currently a per-run generation option passed into `generateGreenMapProducts(options)` so `discoverLidarAssets` can enable only the selected connector(s). Persisting the last selected source per course remains a useful follow-up.
- NRCan hosts HRDEM/CanElevation high-resolution DTM and DSM products under a public FTP/HTTP directory.
- The 1 m DTM root has province/provider folders, including `AB/`, `BC/`, `MB/`, `NB/`, `NL/`, `NS/`, `ON/`, `PEI/`, `QC/`, `SK/`, `YT/`, `NWT/`, and `NU/`, plus municipal/provider folders.
- The HRDEM root also publishes footprint files and product/download documentation:
- PEI's 2020 LiDAR page confirms the operational pattern: raw point cloud data is `.laz`, and derived DTM/aspect/hillshade/slope rasters are published in the federal HRDEM FTP tree.
- PEI's derived DTM path is directly browsable: `https://ftp.maps.canada.ca/pub/elevation/dem_mne/highresolution_hauteresolution/dtm_mnt/1m/PEI/Prince_Edward_Island_2020`.
- Use GDAL/OGR to read the footprint layer and intersect the course bbox.
- Prefer 1 m DTM GeoTIFF assets over raw LAZ for speed and smaller downloads.
- Return only intersecting `dtm_*.tif` assets to the worker.
- For point-cloud mode, use LAZ assets when a DTM is unavailable, but expect larger downloads and slower PDAL processing.

NRCan HRDEM should be Scorecarder's Canada-wide default. It is less elegant than Ontario's ImageServer because discovery requires parsing footprint/index files or directory indexes, but it is open, national, and already contains the PEI data needed for Crowbush.
- This remains the best Ontario integration because the worker can request a TIFF clipped to the exact course/green bbox via ImageServer `exportImage`.
- No additional Ontario work is needed beyond keeping the Ontario bbox guard so it is not used for PEI or other provinces.
Leave Ontario as-is. It should remain the first choice for Ontario courses because it avoids tile index downloads and generates small per-green DTM requests.
- PEI acquired province-wide 2020 LiDAR between 2020-07-15 and 2020-09-15 at point density `>= 6 points / m2` for about `5846.3 km2`.
- Raw point-cloud data exists as `.laz` and is available through Government of Canada Open Data.
- Derived DTM, aspect, hillshade, and slope rasters are available in the federal HRDEM FTP tree.
- The PEI DTM folder includes indexes (`INDEX_utm20_PEI_Prince_Edward_Island_2020.kmz`, `.zip`) and an `utm20/` folder containing tiled GeoTIFF products.
- Implement this first as part of the NRCan HRDEM connector, with a PEI-specific fast path for testing.
- Use the PEI index zip/KMZ to locate intersecting `dtm_*.tif` tiles in `utm20/`.
- Avoid aspect/hillshade/slope rasters for contour generation; use DTM only.
- Validate with The Links at Crowbush Cove before generalizing to other provinces.
This is the best first non-Ontario integration. It directly fixes the Crowbush case and exercises the national HRDEM pattern without needing provincial authentication or custom web-app scraping.
- BC publishes `LidarBC - Open LiDAR Data Portal` in the BC Data Catalogue.
- Open LiDAR Data Portal web app
- The Open LiDAR Data Index is an ArcGIS Feature Service:
- The portal appears designed around indexed public object storage/S3 assets rather than one ImageServer export endpoint.
- Query the FeatureServer layer by course bbox.
- Extract public object-storage URLs from returned attributes.
- Feed LAZ/COPC/GeoTIFF URLs into the existing asset pipeline.
- Prefer DTM/DEM raster products when attributes distinguish them; otherwise use LAZ with PDAL.
BC is very implementable because the open portal exposes an ArcGIS Feature Service index. It needs a connector that understands the BC attribute schema and selects the right asset type.
- Altalis is Alberta's official source for base mapping data and has a `LiDAR 7.5 DEM` product described as a high-accuracy bare-earth DEM created with LiDAR technology.
- Altalis offers a data store with mixed pricing/licensing models, including open data and paid/subscription products.
- GeoDiscover Alberta is an official metadata/search portal and notes catalogue/download workflows, including some FTP links.
- Start with the federal HRDEM `AB/` folder for open, automatable 1 m products where available.
- Treat Altalis as an optional/manual or semi-automated source unless its product endpoints can be accessed without account/cart steps.
- Investigate Altalis product/service API separately before committing to a fully automatic connector.
Alberta can be supported quickly through NRCan HRDEM. Native Altalis integration is likely valuable but riskier because licensing and delivery may not be purely anonymous URL-index based.
- Saskatchewan GeoHub is an ArcGIS Hub-style portal with open-data licensing and public datasets/applications.
- Initial searches did not reveal a unified provincial LiDAR download product comparable to LidarBC or PEI 2020 LiDAR.
- Federal HRDEM has an `SK/` folder, and municipal/provider folders may cover some urban areas.
Implementation feasibility: Medium through federal; low/unknown for provincial LiDAR.
- Use NRCan HRDEM as the default Saskatchewan source.
- Keep a Saskatchewan provincial connector deferred until a reliable tile index or service endpoint is identified.
- Support manual manifests for municipal/regional LiDAR projects.
Do not build a Saskatchewan-specific connector first. Federal HRDEM plus manual manifests is the practical path until a clear provincial LiDAR index is confirmed.
- Manitoba Land Initiative pages are available but difficult to extract automatically from the web fetcher.
- The federal HRDEM tree has an `MB/` folder.
- No clean public API or tile-index endpoint was confirmed during this pass.
Implementation feasibility: Medium through federal; unknown for provincial portal automation.
- Use NRCan HRDEM for Manitoba first.
- Revisit MLI with browser/manual inspection if Manitoba-specific coverage gaps matter.
- Allow direct URL/manifest configuration for MLI downloads if users obtain files manually.
Manitoba should initially ride on the federal connector. A provincial connector should wait until we verify an index format and stable download URL pattern.
- Donnees Quebec has `Données lidar du Québec`.
- LiDAR tile indexes in GPKG and FGDB
- MNT tile indexes in GPKG and FGDB
- Forêt ouverte includes `Produits dérivés issus du lidar` and download/availability index layers.
- Download/cache the MNT index GPKG first; this is the best fit for contour generation.
- Intersect the course bbox against index tiles and resolve download URLs from attributes.
- Use MNT/DTM raster products first, raw LiDAR second.
- Add WMS index only for preview/debug; WMS imagery is not enough for contour generation unless it links to downloadable rasters.
Quebec is one of the best provincial candidates after PEI/NRCan and BC. It exposes explicit downloadable indexes, which are exactly what Scorecarder needs.
- GeoNB has moved to a newer modern website, but the old downloads directory remains browsable for many datasets.
- The top-level downloads directory did not show an obvious `lidar`, `dem`, or `elevation` folder by direct URL guesses in this pass.

# Use executable names on PATH or full paths to your GIS installation.
PDAL_BIN=pdal
GDALINFO_BIN=gdalinfo

GDAL_TRANSLATE_BIN=gdal_translate

GDALDEM_BIN=gdaldem
OGR2OGR_BIN=ogr2ogr
GDALSRSINFO_BIN=gdalsrsinfo
GDALLOCATIONINFO_BIN=gdallocationinfo

# Optional environment root for a conda/contained GDAL and PDAL installation.
GIS_ENV_ROOT=
# Windows browser tests use installed Edge; other platforms use Playwright Chromium.
PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL=msedge

# TerrainServer

Node.js terrain acquisition and local-only serving for Canada and the United States. Select government providers, draw/import a WGS84 boundary or enumerate a whole source, review the acquisition plan, and store immutable files at your chosen destination. A local Leaflet control screen, REST API, STAC search, and Scorecarder-compatible catalog expose the downloaded data.

## Run

Requires Node.js **24+**. There is no transpilation step; the server runs directly from the JavaScript source.

```powershell
npm ci --no-audit --no-fund
npm run check
npm test
npm start
```

The control screen is **http://127.0.0.1:3123/** and interactive API documentation is **http://127.0.0.1:3123/docs**.

The current local [.env](.env) is configured for `C:/Repos/lidarserver/terrain-data` and the existing GDAL/PDAL installation under `C:/Repos/gcsdev/GCS-Dev/Scorecarder/setups/green-tools-env`. That installation is reused without modifying Scorecarder. For another machine, use [.env.example](.env.example) as the configuration reference and adjust the executable and storage paths.

GDAL and PDAL are required for terrain generation and some vector indexes. The GUI's **Repository Settings** shows tool availability. Tools must include GeoTIFF, GeoPackage, Shapefile, LAS/LAZ, and projection support. `GIS_ENV_ROOT` supplies the library, GDAL data, and PROJ paths for a contained environment; projection-network access remains disabled.

Windows browser tests use installed Microsoft Edge. Set `PLAYWRIGHT_CHANNEL` in `.env` for another installed browser channel. On other platforms, install the bundled test browser with `npx playwright install chromium`. Real GIS tests require the configured tools; unavailable toolchains are reported rather than mocked as successful processing.

## First Trial

The repository includes **Ontario Sample Area**, a small, explicitly labeled test area near Toronto, not a claimed golf-course boundary. A real native 0.5 m Ontario DTM was acquired through the GUI. DTM, contours at 0.5/1/2 m intervals, hillshade, and slope were generated locally.

1. Open **Repository** to inspect or download the local files.
2. Open **Courses**, then use the map icon beside Ontario Sample Area to select its boundary.
3. In **Acquire**, choose sources, products, resolutions, delivery/collection options, and a destination. **Discover Files** creates a reviewable plan without downloading terrain files.
4. Review sizes, native grids, coverage, and provider warnings, then download all or selected files. Job details show progress, logs, cancellation, and retry controls.
5. Use the terrain-generation icon in **Courses** to create new, versioned outputs from complete local inputs.

On an empty installation, select **Ontario sample area** from the area selector, then save it as a course. Its zero-meter buffer is intentional for a very small trial. Normal course buffers default to 500 m and can be configured up to 10,000 m.

The map uses bundled country geometry by default. OpenStreetMap is an optional online basemap. Provider discovery/refresh requires Internet access, but existing terrain downloads, previews, elevation/grid queries, and catalogs never contact government services as a fallback.

## Sources And Precision

| Source | Automatic open-data delivery |
| --- | --- |
| Ontario GeoHub | Clipped native 0.5 m DTM exports, DTM/DSM packages, classified point-cloud tile links |
| NRCan CanElevation | HRDEM project and national mosaics, Arctic DEM, CDEM, MRDEM, classified point clouds |
| Prince Edward Island | 2020 native 1 m DTM tiles, federal DTM/DSM surveys, federal point clouds |
| LidarBC | Provincial DEM/DSM and point-cloud indexes; actual per-tile spacing is retained |
| Quebec | Provincial native MNT/DTM tile index plus federal DSM/point-cloud coverage |
| Alberta | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Alberta |
| Nova Scotia | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Nova Scotia |
| Saskatchewan | Open federal CanElevation coverage in Saskatchewan |
| USGS 3DEP | LPC, 1 m/seamless DEMs, published arc-second DEMs, Alaska products, contours |

Alberta/NS/SK account-gated, paid, or unverified provincial delivery is **not** presented as anonymous open downloads. Some Ontario point-cloud tiles require ordering. Coverage is uneven; provider failures and missing anonymous links are recorded in the acquisition plan. Custom ArcGIS, STAC, and vector-index sources can be registered through the GUI or `POST /api/sources` using verified endpoints and attribution.

`GET /api/sources/:id/options` exposes products, collections, formats, delivery modes, known native raster grids, and provider export options. Refreshing provider catalogs adds newly published collection metadata. Provincial choices distinguish native tile grids from dataset scale labels, such as BC's 1:2500 index.

- `best`: prefer the finest known native grid per source/product, retaining coarser tiles needed to fill coverage gaps and point clouds with unknown spacing.
- `all`: retain all published resolutions, deliveries, and survey variants matching the selected products and collections.
- `native`: retain native grids without inventing finer survey precision. Default delivery preferences still apply unless you select collections/delivery explicitly.
- A numeric `resolution`: select a matching native grid; Ontario clipped exports can also request a custom output cell. Finer output cells are explicitly marked **resampled**, not new survey precision.

Raw point-cloud density is not a raster cell size. Unknown spacing/density remains unknown. Meter-grid and angular-resolution products are distinguished. Terrain processing can request arbitrary positive output cells within the configured pixel limit; finer cells interpolate existing observations. Elevation responses retain declared units and vertical-datum provenance. Unknown units are returned as `source units`; no vertical-datum harmonization or inferred unit conversion is performed. `zScale` can explicitly scale point-cloud heights.

Whole-source Ontario acquisition defaults to native packages. Clipped ImageServer exports require an area boundary. Whole-source jobs can be extremely large; inspect known bytes and unknown-size counts before downloading. `MAX_DISCOVERY_ASSETS` and pixel limits fail explicitly instead of silently truncating enumeration or coarsening data. Raise these limits deliberately for larger acquisitions.

## Storage And Jobs

Change the default location through the folder shortcut or Repository Settings. It is persisted to `.env`; all prior roots remain registered and their files are preserved. Each job snapshots its destination. The acquisition form can override the destination for that job without changing the default. Use an absolute local, external-drive, or UNC path with write permission.

```text
terrain-data/
  canada|usa/
    province-or-state|national/
      course-id|repository/
        metadata.json
        course_boundary.geojson
        lidar/raw/<source>-<immutable-asset-id>.laz
        dem/raw/<source>-<immutable-asset-id>.tif
        dem/<processing-job-id>/dtm.tif
        contours/<processing-job-id>/...
        hillshade/<processing-job-id>/...
        slope/<processing-job-id>/...
        generated/jobs/<job-id>/...
        ai/terrain-package-<id>.json
  .indexes/<source>/<revision>/...
```

SQLite stores RTree footprints, metadata, course associations, source options, discovery plans, jobs, logs, and registered file locations. Keep the catalog on a reliable local disk; terrain files may reside on other registered volumes. Back up the catalog and `.env` with the raw data, using a SQLite-aware backup or stopping the server before copying the database and its journal files.

Downloads stream to `.part` files, resume with ETag/Last-Modified and verified range responses, validate signatures/lengths and SHA-256, and publish without overwriting an existing raw path. Provider revisions receive distinct IDs. Copying a catalog asset to another destination retains its previous location. A disconnected volume produces an explicit local-file error; it does not trigger an online fallback.

One durable top-level job runs at a time; downloads use the configured worker concurrency. Running jobs become queued after restart, completed raw files remain intact, and retries resume partial transfers. Cancellation preserves completed and partial files. Interrupted processing may leave working files for inspection; a retry creates a new versioned processing job. Archive extraction preserves the raw ZIP and enforces traversal and uncompressed-size limits. Proprietary ZLAS is downloadable but must be converted externally before processing.

Monthly checks refresh provider metadata and compare validators on acquired assets. They **do not automatically download changed terrain**. `POST /api/jobs/updates` with `downloadChanged: true` explicitly queues changed files. Missing validators are reported as unknown freshness.

Large raw files are streamed; previews use internal overviews or bounded local GDAL windows. Course processing is spatially/pixel bounded, not a whole-country processing batch. This implementation is designed for large repositories, but a 20 TB acquisition/storage stress test has not been performed. Monitor disk space, native-tool memory, and provider limits during large deployments. Catalog byte totals count each current asset once; replicas, index caches, and intermediate working files are additional disk usage.

## REST Examples

Swagger contains request schemas and the full endpoint list. Core routes include:

| Route | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/sources` and `/:id/options` | Cached source metadata and native options |
| `POST /api/discover` | Queue discovery; inspect job result `planId` |
| `GET /api/discovery/:id` | Paginated plan, warnings, native metadata, and all asset IDs |
| `POST /api/downloads` | Download a plan or selected asset IDs |
| `POST /api/acquire` | Explicit discovery and download in one durable job |
| `GET /api/jobs/:id` and `/events` | Status, progress, result, and cursor-based logs |
| `GET/POST /api/courses` | Search/register WGS84 course boundaries |
| `GET /api/course/:id/terrain` | Local DEM/DTM/DSM, contours, hillshade, and slope URLs |
| `GET/POST /api/terrain/query` | Local assets filtered by boundary, source, product, grid, or course |
| `GET /api/assets/:id/download.tif` | Local byte-range/ETag streaming; use the actual extension |
| `POST /api/terrain/elevation` | Up to 1,000 WGS84 `[longitude, latitude]` points |
| `GET /api/terrain/grid?assetId=...` | Up to 512x512 cells, north-to-south, WGS84 cell centers |
| `POST /api/jobs/process` | Generate local course/area terrain products |
| `POST /api/course/:id/package` | Export a persisted AI/hole package with local asset URLs |

PowerShell discovery example:

```powershell
$body = @{
  sourceIds = @('ontario')
  products = @('dtm')
  bbox = @(-79.52, 43.64, -79.519, 43.641)
  bufferMeters = 0
  resolution = 'best'
  delivery = 'export'
  courseId = 'ontario-sample-area'
} | ConvertTo-Json
$job = Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/discover -Method Post -ContentType application/json -Body $body
Invoke-RestMethod "http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/jobs/$($job.id)"
```

Once that job is completed, use its `progress.result.planId` in:

```json
{
  "planId": "<completed-plan-id>",
  "storageRoot": "D:/TerrainData",
  "courseId": "ontario-sample-area",
  "processAfterDownload": true,
  "processing": {
    "products": ["dtm", "contours", "hillshade", "slope"],
    "contourIntervals": [0.5, 1, 2]
  }
}
```

Send that body to `POST /api/downloads`. Incomplete plans are refused unless you explicitly set `allowPartial: true`. Asset query/plan pages use `offset` and `limit` (maximum 1,000); responses include `total` and `nextOffset`. Bboxes accept arrays, comma-separated strings, or Scorecarder's `{minLng,minLat,maxLng,maxLat}` shape. Polygon/MultiPolygon holes are respected. Antimeridian-crossing requests must be split.

Packages can optionally reference a **previously local** satellite asset and include hole, hazards, centerline, or green geometry. There is no satellite acquisition or golf-feature AI inference engine. Packages expose the available terrain and supplied references, not invented geometry.

## Scorecarder Integration

Scorecarder's existing `green-map-worker.js` consumes compatible asset fields and URL extensions. No Scorecarder files were changed. Use its existing configuration hooks:

```dotenv
SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_SOURCE=manual
SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ONTARIO_DTM_ENABLED=false
SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ONTARIO_DTM_PER_GREEN_ENABLED=false
SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_ARCGIS_QUERY_URLS=http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/scorecarder/query
```

Remove other remote ArcGIS/STAC hooks, tile URLs, and old remote manifests when you require the consumer to remain local-only. `manual` avoids its built-in government source discovery; disabling both Ontario flags avoids direct ImageServer exports. The local ArcGIS hook accepts the worker's WGS84 envelope and returns `downloadUrl`, `source`, `title`, `bbox`, `extension`, and `cellSizeMeters`, without a transfer-limit truncation.

Alternative hooks:

- Local STAC: `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_STAC_ENDPOINTS=http://127.0.0.1:3123/api/stac` with optional source collections such as `ontario,nrcan,pei,bc,quebec,usgs-3dep,derived`.
- Manifest: obtain `GET /api/scorecarder/manifest?bbox=...` or `GET /api/course/:id/manifest`, follow pagination when applicable, and pass the JSON to its existing `SCORECARDS_GREEN_MAP_LIDAR_MANIFEST_JSON` or manifest-file hook. The hook expects JSON/file contents, not a remote manifest URL.

Acquire the requested course/green area first. The consumer receives only complete local processable TIFF/LAS/LAZ assets; ZIP/ZLAS/IMG can remain raw and need extraction/conversion as appropriate. Finer Scorecarder output cells do not imply finer source surveys.

The existing consumer hooks do not add TerrainServer Bearer headers automatically. The default loopback/no-key configuration works directly. When enabling `API_KEY`, add authenticated requests in the consumer or use a trusted authenticated integration layer; do not put an API key into a catalog URL. Direct browser clients also need their actual origin added to `CORS_ORIGINS`. Server-to-server requests are not subject to browser CORS.

## Security And Operations

Loopback binding is the default. A non-loopback `HOST` requires `API_KEY`, and authenticated callers can browse storage paths and queue downloads, so treat that key as administrative access. Bind behind TLS and firewall restrictions for remote use. The GUI keeps the key only in page memory; downloaded-file tickets expire after ten minutes. API definition/health and static frontend assets are public, but repository data/settings require Bearer authentication when enabled.

Download destinations are checked against registered roots and real paths. Public-source network requests reject private/reserved IPs, unexpected hosts/ports, embedded credentials, and unsafe redirects, with validated DNS connection addresses. `DOWNLOAD_ALLOWED_HOSTS` extends the government/public-infrastructure allowlist. `ALLOW_PRIVATE_DOWNLOAD_HOSTS` is an explicit development/trusted-internal exception; do not enable it for untrusted callers. Native tools are spawned directly without a shell. Provider content is data, not executable instructions.

Keep provider attribution with reused raw and derived data. `.env`, the terrain/index files, catalogs, dependencies, and logs are ignored by Git. Do not delete registered raw files to free space without accounting for dependent course/derived manifests. Shut down with Ctrl+C so the current job is persisted for restart.

  - Inspect the consumer at `C:\Repos\gcsdev\GCS-Dev\Scorecarder` and provide compatible interfaces, without modifying it.
  - “You are on autopilot... build and run the application, testing as you go, until you've got something ready for me to try.”
  - Required development/service default port: **3123**. Node hosting. Configuration in **.env**.
  - Latest substantive request: **“also create a setup program to install this new service using an installer... this is so the service can easily be installed and configured on any server I choose...”**
- Workspace: `C:\Repos\lidarserver`, initially only `plan.md`. Windows. Current date supplied: 2026-10-31.
- User unavailable for clarification:
  - Asked Windows/Windows+Linux/Linux and bundled/downloaded prerequisites.
  - Both tool answers: **“The user is not available to respond and will review your work later. Work autonomously and make good decisions.”**
  - Agent decision announced: **self-contained Windows/x64 installer plus Linux/x64 systemd installation path**.
  - This installer decision is a plan, not implemented or verified yet.
- No Scorecarder files changed. No commits or branches. No subagents used. Do not finish until installer and final verification are handled.

Applicable Working Instructions:
- Start/resume with concise commentary and preface each tool batch with a one-sentence purpose/outcome update.
- Give progress after 3–5 calls or about every 30 seconds.
- Use `functions.apply_patch` for manual edits. No shell-write tricks or Python file manipulation.
- **The patch implementation rejects duplicate Update File paths within one patch.** Use one file header with multiple `@@` sections, despite conflicting examples in developer text.
- After a substantive edit, immediately run focused executable validation; do not read widely or continue patching first.
- Honor persistent preference for full/fresh test validation. ESM has no transpilation build; final gates should include fresh `npm ci`, full `npm test`, syntax check.
- Do not revert user changes or raw data, commit, branch, or install privileged services without proper authorization. No subagents unless explicitly permitted.
- Windows terminal is PowerShell. Inline Node ESM:
  ```
  @'
  ...JavaScript...
  '@ | node --input-type=module
  ```
- `rg` unavailable; workspace file tools work. External source files can be read directly with `read_file`.
- Sync commands for one-shot tasks. Async only for persistent servers. Do not poll/sleep terminal executions.
- Do not trigger interactive elevation/UAC with `RunAs`; for privileged installation tests use a deliberate non-elevated/test mode or instruct user to run the real privileged installer later.
- Must visually verify desktop/mobile UI, leave application available on3123, disclose untested installer/platform limits.
- `task_complete` only after all work/verification and brief summary. Do not call during this handoff.
- Memories viewed: `/memories/build-preferences.md`, `/memories/debugging.md` exist; session/repo memory empty. No new memory written.
- Skill previously read: project-setup-info-local. Newly listed .NET skills do not apply to this Node application.
- Original user plan unchanged.

2. Technical Foundation:
- Node **v24.14.1**, ESM, `engines` Node>=24.
- Express5, built-in `node:sqlite` `DatabaseSync` (experimental warning expected).
- Dependencies in package.json:
  - @fontsource/ibm-plex-sans ^5.2.0
  - @terraformer/arcgis ^2.2.0

- Scripts:

- Architecture:
  - Acquisition/discovery/update jobs contact providers.
  - Terrain serving, file access, previews, elevation/grid, STAC and Scorecarder catalogs are **local-only**, no public fallback.

Core modules:

  - Network response/json/text/download, publicAddress, fileHash, publishFile.

  - projection helpers and Gis env/run/check.

- `src/indexes.js`:
  - structured HTML links, resolution attributes, Canadian host canonicalization.

Frontend:

A local Leaflet control screen, REST API, STAC search, and Scorecarder-compatible catalog expose the downloaded data. + +## Install On A Server + +Ready-to-run packages: + +- Windows/x64: [dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-windows-x64-setup.exe](dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-windows-x64-setup.exe). +- Linux/x64: [dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-linux-x64-setup.run](dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-linux-x64-setup.run). +- Companion GIS source bundles: [dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-windows-x64-gis-sources.tar.gz](dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-windows-x64-gis-sources.tar.gz) and [dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-linux-x64-gis-sources.tar.gz](dist/TerrainServer-1.0.0-linux-x64-gis-sources.tar.gz). + +Each installer contains Node.js 24 LTS, production JavaScript dependencies, GDAL 3.13.2, PDAL 2.10.2, CRS data, and original third-party license notices. Confirm native binary compatibility on other distributions before deployment. + +### Windows + +Run the setup executable on the target server. Choose **all users** for a Windows service, then select the program directory, persistent state directory, default terrain storage, port (default **3123**), bind address, and authentication. Defaults are: + +```text +C:\Program Files\TerrainServer program and bundled runtimes +C:\ProgramData\TerrainServer\.env protected service configuration +C:\ProgramData\TerrainServer\catalog SQLite catalog +C:\ProgramData\TerrainServer\logs rotated service logs +C:\ProgramData\TerrainServer\terrain-data default terrain destination +``` + +The optional `TerrainServer` Windows service uses the unprivileged **LocalService** account, automatic delayed startup, restart-on-failure, and rotated logs. The installer grants that account access to the selected dedicated state/storage directories. A UNC share requires an explicitly configured domain/service account with share and filesystem permissions; LocalService is not an authenticated network-share identity. No firewall ports are opened automatically. + +The **current user** install mode requires no elevation and creates a foreground-launch shortcut, not a system service. Unattended current-user installation example: + +```powershell +.\dist\TerrainServer-1.0.0-windows-x64-setup.exe /CURRENTUSER /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /DIR="C:\TerrainServer\Program" /STATEDIR="C:\TerrainServer\State" /STORAGEROOT="D:\TerrainData" /PORT=3123 /BIND=127.0.0.1 +``` + +For unattended service installation, an administrator uses `/ALLUSERS` instead of `/CURRENTUSER`. `/REQUIREKEY=1` generates a key even for loopback.
